name: Rise : sleep tracker
tagline: Tracks sleep debt and predicts your daily energy peaks and dips from your circadian rhythm.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The math here is less mysterious than the marketing suggests: sleep debt is a rolling 14-day sum of how far each night fell short of your estimated need, and the energy curve is a sine-ish function anchored to your average sleep midpoint. An agent can read that data straight out of HealthKit and compute both in a session, and the resulting chart will track Rise's fairly closely most weeks. What you cannot one-shot is the packaging: a phone app you actually open every morning, notifications that fire at the right minute, and the years of tuning that make their sleep-need estimate feel personal rather than a formula. You also need a Mac, Xcode, and a signing identity before anything lands on your wrist or home screen. Buildable, genuinely useful, and noticeably rougher than the thing you are replacing.
coreLoopDIY: Pulls your nightly sleep from HealthKit, computes a rolling 14-day sleep debt against an estimated sleep need, and draws today's predicted energy peaks and dips anchored to your recent sleep midpoint.
requirements: An iPhone with sleep data in Apple Health, ideally from a watch or ring
A free Apple developer account for on-device signing, re-signed every 7 days without a paid one
At least two weeks of existing sleep history for the debt number to mean anything
whatYouLose: Rise's tuned personal sleep-need estimate, which is the one number the whole app hangs on
Reliable, well-timed notifications for melatonin window, caffeine cutoff, and peak windows
Android, iPad, and any hope of a widget you did not build yourself
Their habit and behavior-change content, which is the part that actually changes behavior
Someone else fixing it when HealthKit changes its sleep stage schema
moatNotes: The circadian science is public; the calibration of sleep need per user across millions of nights is not, and that is the number everything else is derived from.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a sleep app that does not nag you at the right moment is just a chart, and charts do not fix bedtimes. Rise wins on timing and tone: it tells you to stop drinking coffee at 1:42pm, not to consult a graph. People also pay because they want a confident personalized sleep-need number rather than a formula they typed in themselves, and because the app is polished enough to survive the first boring week, which is where every DIY health tracker dies.
notes: The formula is a weekend; the nagging is the product.
prompt:
Build a single-screen iOS app called DebtClock that tracks sleep debt and predicted daily energy from Apple Health data.

Stack, non-negotiable: Swift 5.9+, SwiftUI, HealthKit, Swift Charts, iOS 17 minimum. One Xcode project, no Swift packages, no backend, no accounts, no analytics, no network calls at all. Everything computes on device.

Setup:
- Create the Xcode project structure and an Info.plist with NSHealthShareUsageDescription explaining read-only sleep access.
- Enable the HealthKit entitlement. Request read access to HKCategoryTypeIdentifier.sleepAnalysis only. Never request write access.

Core logic in a SleepModel type:
- Query the last 21 days of sleepAnalysis samples. Merge overlapping samples from multiple sources, preferring the source with the most granular stage data.
- Collapse samples into nightly sessions: group by the night they belong to, where a night runs from noon to noon.
- For each night compute total asleep time, excluding inBed and awake stages.
- Sleep need: default 8h 10m, user-adjustable with a stepper in 10 minute steps, persisted in UserDefaults. Do not pretend to estimate it, label the field "your guess" in the UI.
- Sleep debt: sum of max(0, need - asleep) over the trailing 14 nights, capped display at 20 hours. Show it in hours and minutes.
- Sleep midpoint: circular mean of the last 7 nights' midpoints, handled correctly across midnight.
- Energy curve: a function of time-of-day producing 0 to 100, built as a cosine with its trough about 2 hours before the sleep midpoint plus a secondary afternoon dip roughly 7 hours after wake, then scaled down linearly by current sleep debt.

UI, one scrolling screen:
- Big sleep debt number at top with a one-line plain-language read.
- A Swift Chart of today's energy curve with a now marker, shaded peak windows where energy is above 70 and dip windows below 45.
- Derived times listed as rows: melatonin window start, caffeine cutoff, suggested bedtime. Derive these from the midpoint with fixed offsets and label them as heuristics, not medical advice.
- A bar chart of the last 14 nights, asleep hours versus the need line.
- An empty state that says exactly which permission or data is missing.

Also include:
- Local notifications for caffeine cutoff and bedtime, scheduled daily, toggleable, requested only after the user taps the toggle.
- Unit tests for the nightly grouping, the 14-day debt sum, and the circular midpoint mean, including a night that crosses DST.

Out of scope, do not build: cloud sync, widgets, Apple Watch target, onboarding flow, any sleep staging model, any claim of clinical accuracy. Add a README with build steps, the exact HealthKit permission path in Settings, and a note that free provisioning profiles expire after 7 days.
